text: Machine learning is a way for computers to learn from data without being explicitly programmed. One common type is supervised learning, where the computer uses training data that includes both inputs and correct answers. For example, if we show it photos of cats and dogs labeled correctly, the system learns to identify patterns. Based on this training, it builds a model—a mathematical rule or set of rules—that can then make predictions on new, unseen photos. After training, we test the model on fresh data to measure its accuracy, which tells us how often the predictions are correct. The goal is to improve the model until its predictions are reliable enough for real-world tasks.
